newsitem.title: USA: Fed seen adding via multi-day system repurchases.
newsitem.headline: Fed seen adding via multi-day system repurchases.

text.p: The Federal Reserve is likely to add temporary reserves to the banking system on Thursday via multi-day system repurchase agreements, analysts said.
"I'm looking for a term system RP -- probably a six-day but a 14-day operation is also possible," said Patricia Thrapp, vice president at Aubrey G. Lanston & Co.
"A six-day operation would stay on the Fed's books until Tuesday, the settlement date for the (Treasury's) refunding, so they might decide to do it until Tuesday," she said.

Thrapp said the Fed has a "very large add need" of $8.0 billion on average for the week, rising to $10.5 billion to a daily average of $10.0 billion in the second half of the bank reserve maintenance period.
Analysts also said that with the Fed's add need expected to grow, the open market desk could add permanent reserves to the banking system through a coupon pass at any time.
"The (seasonal) add need is growing more quickly this year partly because the Fed didn't do a coupon pass in November and December," said Thrapp.
Analysts at MMS International Inc also expect the Fed to add temporary reserves to the banking system on Thursday.

"We expect the Fed to intervene with term system repos today to address the add need over the holiday weekend," MMS said. The Presidents Day holiday is this Monday and banks and financial markets will be closed to mark the occasion.
The Treasury market will also close three hours early on Friday in advance of the holiday weekend.
"Our reserve projections show the need to supplement the 14-day rps announced last week," the MMS analysts said.
In mid-morning dealings, Federal funds were trading at 5-1/4 percent, the Fed's target for the rate.
(( -- E. Freilich, North American Treasury Desk 212-859-1679))
